the EGF-displaying helper phagemid particles can be used to package the pSilencer1-siEGFP or pSilencer4-siAkt plamids to deliver siEGFP or siAkt to cells and to down-regulate the target genes EGFP or Akt.
the EGF-displaying M13 phagemids can be used as an effective RNA interference system in the presence of hydroxycamptotecin.
phagemid particles can be used to deliver siRNA to cells and that the gene expression can be downregulated efficiently by RNA interference.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an effective RNA interference system using the EGF ligand-displaying phagemids.
the application of phagemid particles for gene therapy.
the development of a novel siRNA delivery system, which will be of value in the study of gene function and in gene therapy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the phagemid RNAi vectors can be packaged efficiently by the modified helper phage M13KO7-EGFCT and the gene transduction of siRNA is enhanced in the presence of the chemotherapeutic drug HCPT.
the RNAi vectors can be packaged by phagemid particles and the RNAi effect is enhanced by the presence of the ligand.
the phagemid particle-based siRNA delivery system is a potential approach for gene therapy.

we have developed a new RNA interference system using a phagemid particles-displaying EGF ligand.
the phagemid particle can be used as an efficient RNAi vector for gene therapy.
the phagemid particle is a promising vector for gene therapy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the phagemid particle system may be an efficient and safe siRNA delivery vector for RNAi-based cancer therapy.
the phagemid particle can be used for RNA interference in the absence of a helper virus.
phagemid-encoding RNAi vectors can be packaged and delivered to the target cells in the form of EGF-displaying particles.
